column1: # What a C++ istringstream does for `i >> M >> k >> roff >> bc;` (four `unsigned int`, default flags) on the lines of the optimized
# ascii counts file's hash parameter line (blastn -window_masker_taxid; NCBI's CSeqMaskerIstatOAscii reads line 3 of its header so).
# Written 2026-11-20 by `g++ -O1 -o uint_probe uint_probe.cpp` and `./uint_probe < lines.in`, with lines.in = `python3 gen_lines.py` (both here).
# 3,038 of the 3,046 rows were run on ws with g++ 11.4.0 (Ubuntu 22.04) and again with g++ 13.3.0 (Ubuntu 24.04), both with the system
# libstdc++.so.6: the two tables are identical. The last 8 rows (the lines of the blastn freezes that the first 3,038 did not hold) were
# run with 13.3.0 only (ws was down). The official blastn 2.17.0 is a GCC 8.5 build with its own libstdc++: it is tied to this table by the
# cases taxid_oascii_uint_* of tests/fixtures/winmask_blastn/cases.tsv (REPORT.md of line LIB-O item O1d lists which row each one covers).
# Columns: line (escapes \t \n \r \v \f \0 \\ \xHH), then M, k, roff, bc (`-`: the stream left the variable unchanged), then the
# stream's state after the reads (g good, e eof, f fail, b bad).
